title: Etale sum-extension sheaf projection formula
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $e:V\to T$ be a separated étale morphism of finite type of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $M$ and $N$ be sheaves of $A$-modules on the small étale sites of $V$ and $T$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use exact inverse image $e^*=e^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For the sheafified lift-indexed sum extension $e_{\Sigma!}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], the assignment on a test object $W\to T$
$$
(s,m)\otimes n\longmapsto(s,m\otimes s^*n),
$$
where $s:W\to V$ is a lift ($e\circ s$ is the structure map of $W$), $m\in M(W,s)$, $n\in N(W)$, and $s^*n\in(e^*N)(W,s)$ is the image of $n$ under the unit $N(W)\to(e^{-1}N)(V\times_TW)$ followed by restriction along the graph $(s,\mathrm{id}_W):W\to V\times_TW$, induces a canonical natural isomorphism of sheaves
$$
p^0_{M,N}:e_{\Sigma!}M\otimes_A N\xrightarrow{\sim}e_{\Sigma!}(M\otimes_A e^*N).
$$
It is compatible with restrictions and $A$-balancing. At a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, under the stalk formula for $e_{\Sigma!}$ [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks], the tensor-stalk identification [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] and the inverse-image stalk identification $(e^*N)_{\bar v}\cong N_{\bar t}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], it is the direct-sum map
$$
\left(\bigoplus_{\bar v\mapsto\bar t}M_{\bar v}\right)\otimes_A N_{\bar t}\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{\bar v\mapsto\bar t}(M_{\bar v}\otimes_A N_{\bar t})
$$
with the displayed component formula.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection): its pure-tensor construction (Z,s)\otimes t\mapsto(Z,s\otimes f^{-1}t) and geometric-stalk square, adapted from the finite-support model f_{p!} to the lift-indexed sum model of a separated etale finite-type morphism (the two models are identified by the graph sections of etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F4L); compare sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), which gives only an abstract Yoneda isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $P_M(W)=\bigoplus_{s:W\to V/T}M(W,s)$, $Q=M\otimes_Ae^*N$, and $H=e_{\Sigma!}Q$. These are the defining sum presheaves and sheaf tensor product. For each lift $s$, put $u_s(n)=\Gamma_s^*\eta_e(W)(n)$, where $\Gamma_s=(s,\mathrm{id}_W)$. The constant-coefficient inverse-image adjunction is an adjunction of module sheaves, so $u_s$ is $A$-linear. The rule $b_W(\sum_s\iota_sm_s,n)=\sum_s\eta_{P_Q,W}(\iota_s(m_s\otimes u_s(n)))$ is therefore $A$-bilinear. All sums are finite; the formula respects addition in every summand and $b_W(a\iota_sm,n)=b_W(\iota_sm,an)$. For a test morphism $h:W'\to W$, the graph identity $(\mathrm{id}_V\times h)\Gamma_{sh}=\Gamma_sh$, naturality of the unit, and the restriction maps in the defining sum and tensor presheaves give $u_s(n)|_{(W',sh)}=u_{sh}(n|_{W'})$. Thus restricting $b_W(\iota_sm,n)$ gives exactly $b_{W'}(\iota_{sh}(m|_{W'}),n|_{W'})$, including when several lifts restrict to the same lift (their entries add). This constructs a bilinear morphism of presheaves $P_M\times N\to H$.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), pure-tensor construction and restriction check; lift-indexed model as in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S5 (proposition-describe-jshriek)

proof.text: Apply the bilinear sheafification-extension theorem with ring presheaf the constant presheaf $A$, its sheafification $A_T$, presheaves $\mathcal F=P_M$ and $\mathcal G=N$, and target $\mathcal H=H$. The theorem extends $b$ uniquely to an $A_T$-bilinear morphism $(P_M)^\#\times N\to H$; here $N^\#=N$ canonically by the sheafification universal property because $N$ is already a sheaf. The sheaf tensor universal property then gives a unique module morphism $p^0_{M,N}:(P_M)^\#\otimes_{A_T}N\to H$. The defining sum extension identifies $(P_M)^\#=e_{\Sigma!}M$, and its unit equation reads $p^0(\eta_{P_M}(\iota_sm)\otimes n)=\eta_{P_Q}(\iota_s(m\otimes u_s(n)))$. This is precisely the formula asserted in the statement. Notice that the extension theorem supplies a bilinear map, and the separate tensor universal property supplies the linear map out of the sheaf tensor.

source.place: Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), bilinear extension and the Hom–Bilin display immediately following it in Section 03EK

proof.text: For module morphisms $a:M\to M'$ and $c:N\to N'$, both naturality composites send $(\iota_sm)\otimes n$ to $\iota_s(a(m)\otimes u_s(c(n)))$: naturality of the unit gives $e^*c(u_s(n))=u_s(c(n))$. The uniqueness in bilinear extension, followed by injectivity of the Hom–Bilin bijection, identifies the two sheaf morphisms. Restriction compatibility and balancing were verified for $b$ in Step 1 and are preserved by its bilinear extension and tensor factorization. Thus the constructed map is canonical and natural in both variables.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), compatibility with restrictions and naturality of the pure-tensor construction

proof.text: Fix $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$. The sum-stalk formula identifies the germ of $\iota_sm$, represented on a pointed neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$, with $m_{\bar v}$ in the summand $\bar v=s\bar w$. The tensor-stalk formula identifies its tensor with $n_{\bar t}$ with the germ of $\eta_{P_M}(\iota_sm)\otimes n$. By Step 2 its image is the germ of $\iota_s(m\otimes u_s(n))$, which the target sum-stalk and tensor-stalk formulas send to $m_{\bar v}\otimes(u_s(n))_{\bar v}$. The graph $\Gamma_s$ maps the pointed neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar v$ into $(V\times_TW,(\bar v,\bar w))$, so restricting the unit image along this pointed morphism does not change its germ. The inverse-image stalk-germ theorem therefore sends $(u_s(n))_{\bar v}$ to $n_{\bar t}$. This identification is $A$-linear: its naturality for multiplication-by-$a$ endomorphisms of $N$ gives scalar compatibility for each $a\in A$. Consequently the actual map $(p^0_{M,N})_{\bar t}$ becomes $D:(\bigoplus_{\bar v\mapsto\bar t}M_{\bar v})\otimes_AN_{\bar t}\to\bigoplus_{\bar v\mapsto\bar t}(M_{\bar v}\otimes_AN_{\bar t})$, $D(\iota_{\bar v}m\otimes n)=\iota_{\bar v}(m\otimes n)$. These generators determine the map because the stalk and tensor identifications are isomorphisms and ordinary tensors are generated by pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), geometric-stalk square; etale-cohomology.tex Tags 03S5 and 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), including the germ formula

proof.text: For each $\bar v$, the bilinear map $(m,n)\mapsto\iota_{\bar v}m\otimes n$ induces a linear map $M_{\bar v}\otimes_AN_{\bar t}\to(\bigoplus M_{\bar v})\otimes_AN_{\bar t}$ by the module tensor universal property. Adding these maps on finite-support tuples defines $E$ on $\bigoplus(M_{\bar v}\otimes_AN_{\bar t})$. Then $DE$ fixes every $\iota_{\bar v}(m\otimes n)$ and $ED$ fixes every $\iota_{\bar v}m\otimes n$. These generate their respective modules, so both composites are identities. Hence the stalk map $D$ is invertible, with no finiteness or flatness assumption on the modules.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), elementary verification that the lower horizontal direct-sum tensor map is an isomorphism; algebra.tex Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: Every geometric stalk of $p^0_{M,N}$ is an isomorphism by Steps 4–5. The conservativity theorem for geometric stalks makes the underlying morphism of abelian sheaves an isomorphism. Its inverse is $A$-linear since the original bijective morphism is $A$-linear, so it is an isomorphism of $A$-module sheaves. Together with Step 3 and the calculation of Step 4 this proves every clause, including the specified map on geometric stalks.
